§5I’ve§0 found nothing else to write about in §6Arches of Yarn§0. 

After the first thing §5I’ve§0 written, the urge to make has depleted entirely. 

It couldn’t even be bothered to leave a note explaining itself.

§5I§0 attempted to write

some more, but couldn’t even form the first words.

Nothing in this stairway is inspiring to §5me§0 now. 

Instead, these steps make §5me§0 feel rather weary. 

Or rather, not the stairs themselves, but

some other pervasive force. 

Something much worse than those awful, darker-than-pitch veils at either end of the stairs is beginning to build up, and it threatens to take §5me§0 over. 

Gone is the relief of the silence, the

jubilance of 
§5my§0 isolation. 

A terrible sensation that plagues the very air §5I§0 breathe has taken respite here. 

Its vampiric essence sucking out every drop of energy in §5my§0 muscles. 

§5I§0 thought perhaps it

was just the activity of climbing the stairs building this up, but even after stopping to rest for a moment, it has only grown. 

Heat. 

For some reason, it’s started to get very hot in the stairs.

§5I§0 noticed some time

ago, 
hours?, 
seconds?, 
minutes?, 

it doesn’t matter how long. 

The closest thing to a clock to gauge §5my §0time here is the number of times §5I’ve§0 lost count of the steps §5I’ve§0 gone up.

While §5my§0 time so far here has been rather pleasant, the lack of distractions and noise allows §5my§0 mind to run free with ideas–it seems §5I§0 was very much a writer before having §5my§0 mind and memory taken from me–this heat is changing that view.
It’s a sick, cruel §4§lbeast§0, this heat.

§5I§0 can’t begin to understand where it’s coming from. 

While §5I§0 can’t say for sure that the temperature was pleasant, or even perhaps cold, it is undeniably sweltering now. 

Where is this heat even coming from?

There’s no 
obvious source. 

This stairway isn’t particularly long, and the looping nature means §5I§0 would have seen some kind of vent for the air to come in from.

§5I§0 don’t particularly care where it’s coming from, though.

§5I’d§0 rather it just not be here at all. 

§5I’ve§0 begun to sweat, §5my§0 body’s desperate attempt to cool §5me§0 down from this awful incalescence. 

What has started as just a handful of sweat beads has been strung into a rather disgusting pearly

necklace. The sleeves of §5my§0 coat become slick as §5I§0 wipe §5my§0 forehead on them. 

Likewise, §5my§0 hands become equally drenched, and it becomes cumbersome to hold onto 
§6Arches of Yarn§0. 

§5I§0 feel like a melting candle. This is fucking

unbearable. 

What the hell 
is going on? 

Why is this happening? How is this happening? 
Everything was 
fine before, and suddenly it’s absolutely insufferable.

Something strange 
is going on. 

Wait. 

It’s now 
dawning 
on §5me§0. 

While §5I§0 feel science isn’t a particularly deep interest of §5mine§0, §5I§0 certainly understand it enough

to know a very important fact of heat. 
Something that’s making §5me§0 partially regret §5my§0 choice to climb so much up these stairs. 

Something that makes no sense, and throws §5me§0 back into the abyss of not understanding.

Heat rises. 

Density is a measure of how much stuff is in a given area. 

Energy makes 
things expand. 

More energy, more heat, means the same amount of stuff in a larger area; more energy means lower

density. 

Hot air rises and cold air sinks because hot air is thinner, less dense, than cold air. 

But this doesn’t 
make any sense. 

Why is it getting hotter as §5I§0 go up, if §5I’ve§0 already made it clear that §5I§0 am in such a

small, closed loop? 

Does this mean that despite being on this ontological treadmill, §5I’m§0 somehow still moving up on some grander stage? 

From §5my§0 estimates, there’s only about 550 steps, which takes §5me§0 about 8 minutes to climb.

Somehow, though, despite being trapped in such a space, §5I§0 am continuing to progress after all.

This growing heat is an indication of that.

But what am §5I§0 progressing towards?

Is something at the top waiting for §5me§0?

What if this 
heat is a 
deterrent? 

Something terrible sits at the top, desperate to get its hands on §5me§0. 
This heat is a warning, telling §5me§0 to leave before §5I§0 find out what it’ll do when it gets §5me§0.

But then, §5who§0 is

warning §5me§0? 

Is this naturally attached to whatever §4§lbeast§0 rests at the top, or is something else warning §5me§0? 

No. 

Stop that.

Look at §5me§0, inventing §4§lbeast§0s to speculate

on because of an uncomfortable scenario. 

Unable to be content with the idea that things are simply uncomfortable, §5I’m§0 fabricating folktales out of §5who§0lecloth.

Stitching and weaving together a spool of word-thread into a

broad quilted story to wrap §5myself§0 in. 



§lThere is no such thing as monsters. §0

No §4§lbeast§0 sits at the top of these stairs. 

§5I§0 must accept that §5I§0 am alone in this

stairway. 

The only monstrous force §5I§0 have to deal with is this calefaction of the air §5I§0 breathe.
